requirement:
`ValidationCache::usage()` returns an owned snapshot of the cache’s lifetime
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.UsageStats`. A newly constructed
cache starts at zero. Every agent call through the cache or any clone adds its
usage exactly once by the time the call returns, including retries and failed
attempts. Concurrent calls contribute to the same totals. The snapshot sums tool invocations and result bytes by tool name across validators under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.ToolUsage.by_name`. Reading a snapshot
preserves the counters, and later calls leave earlier snapshots unchanged.

```rust,ignore
impl<D: Domain> ValidationCache<D> {
    pub fn usage(&self) -> UsageStats;
}
```
rationale:
Obligations from `requirements.sdk.validation-cache.usage`, mapped to the marked tests:

- **Starts at zero.** `agent_executions_isolate_conversations_and_dependency_traces` takes `cache.usage()` before any call. It asserts `initial.attempts == 0` and empty `tools`. The cache is also read after the calls, and `initial` is rechecked at the end, so the zero start is checked. `validators_keep_measured_tokens_after_failed_attempts_and_evidence_reuse` checks all counters and token categories on a fresh `Validator`'s usage, which is a different object from the cache.
- **Each call is added exactly once, including retries and failed attempts.**
  - `validators_keep_measured_tokens_after_failed_attempts_and_evidence_reuse` runs a throttled failure, a retry that succeeds, then a terminal failure. It asserts `graph.cache().usage()` has attempts 3, retries 1, failed_attempts 2, and the expected token and missing_attempts values. It also asserts that evidence reuse (`refresh_evidence`) adds nothing.
  - `cache_retains_usage_across_validators_and_sums_each_token_category` asserts attempts 3, retries 1, failed_attempts 1, and exact per-category token sums.
  - `dropping_an_inflight_request_preserves_its_attempt` asserts the cache keeps the attempt (1, 0, 1) when the call is dropped before it returns.
- **Through the cache or any clone.** `cache_retains_usage_across_validators_and_sums_each_token_category` uses `graph`, a clone `peer`, and a cloned `cache`. It asserts that all three views report the same total of 3 attempts.
- **Concurrent calls share totals.** `agent_executions_isolate_conversations_and_dependency_traces` uses `futures::join!` with a barrier that needs both conversations in flight. It asserts `cache.usage().attempts == 6`, which is the sum of the two validators' 3 each.
- **Tool calls and result bytes are summed by name across validators.** The same test asserts, for `read_node`, `get_next_page` and `submit_result`, that the cache totals equal the two validators' values. Calls are 1 + 1 = 2, and result_bytes is the sum of the two validators' bytes. It also asserts the cache has exactly 3 tool entries. This covers the cited `ToolUsage.by_name` for built-in tools. A separate test in `configured.rs`, `registered_tools_use_the_current_context_and_ordinary_node_ids`, also reads `cache().usage().tools` for registered tools. It is not marked for this requirement. I did not treat that as a gap, because the summing is the same for built-in and registered tools.
- **Owned snapshot, reading preserves counters, earlier snapshots are unchanged.** `initial` (attempts 0, empty tools) is still unchanged after later calls. `before_failure` (read before the failing call) still has `failed_attempts == 1` after the later calls. Repeated `cache.usage()` reads give consistent totals.

The cited `UsageStats` fields (prepared and delivered inputs, token counts) are also asserted at the cache level. I found no unacknowledged gap.

text: `ValidationCache::usage()` returns an owned snapshot of the cache’s lifetime
cache starts at zero. Every agent call through the cache or any clone adds its
usage exactly once by the time the call returns, including retries and failed

attempts. Concurrent calls contribute to the same totals. The snapshot sums tool invocations and result bytes by tool name across validators under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.ToolUsage.by_name`. Reading a snapshot
preserves the counters, and later calls leave earlier snapshots unchanged.

`UsageStats` exposes the following totals. `attempts` counts each request sent to the provider once. `retries` counts attempts that repeat a failed request. `failed_attempts` counts attempts that returned a provider error, including those followed by a successful retry.

`prepared_inputs` counts inputs prepared for agent messages. Each node inserted in the opening message counts once. Each requested `read_node` page and each `outgoing_edges` result counts once, including repeated reads. A requested search page counts one input per excerpt on that page. Source listings, search finalization, and opaque custom-tool results contribute zero.

`delivered_inputs` counts those inputs when the provider first responds successfully to the request carrying them. Each input counts once across retries and subsequent turns that replay the same conversation history. For example, if the opening message supplies three nodes and the provider fails permanently before replying, usage records three prepared inputs and zero delivered inputs.
`UsageStats::tools` starts empty and holds one entry per invoked tool, keyed by name. This includes built-in and registered tools.
